headline: All majors below the 200-day line; funding still positive and longs crowded; whales moving BTC off exchange while stables flood in for leverage
paragraphs: The regime is uniformly bearish. All seven tracked assets sit below their 200-day simple moving average, and none have printed a golden cross. Bitcoin trades 48.7% below its 12-month high at 63,947; Ethereum sits 61.1% underwater; the secondary names show even worse drawdowns, with XRP off 69%, SOL off 69.2%, and DOGE off 75.9%. The only outlier on momentum is BNB, whose RSI-14 sits at 60.7, technically elevated, but that occurs against a price that has already lost 54.2% of its range and shows no cross to confirm a regime shift. For the rest, momentum is either neutral (Bitcoin's RSI at 48.5, Ethereum and XRP in the 36 to 50 band) or resting, while the underlying trend has been down for months. This is a bear market with no technical evidence of reversal.

The one source of lift on the tape is a narrow pulse of positive MACD state. Bitcoin, Solana, BNB, ADA, and DOGE all show MACD above signal line, suggesting the immediate downward momentum may be pausing or consolidating, yet that message is incomplete. Ethereum and XRP both show MACD below signal, and Ethereum's 24-hour decline of 1.87% despite RSI at the midpoint (50.0) is a quiet divergence: price fell without momentum confirmation. More telling is the disconnect between recent price action and the deeper trend: Bitcoin is up 1.67% over seven days and 7.48% over 30 days, while still 48.7% from the 12-month peak. That recovery is a relief bounce in a bear market, not a regime flip. Volatility across the board remains elevated (Bitcoin at 28.1%, Ethereum at 39.7%, ADA at the extreme of 59.4%), which is the sound of indecision.

Derivatives paint a picture of sustained long bias at elevated cost. Bitcoin funding stands at 0.01% per 8 hours (11.0% annualized), ETH at 0.0093% (10.2% annualized), and the smaller caps all priced at 11.0%. These are not panic lows, but they are not cheap. The long-to-short ratio on Bitcoin is 1.35, on ETH 1.78, on Solana 2.0, and on XRP 3.69, with DOGE at the extreme of 5.25 longs for every short. This concentration of bullish leverage is the structural condition to watch: it says the derivative market believes in a rebound, and it will pay premium to hold that bet. Open interest is substantial (Bitcoin at 2.04 billion USD, ETH at 1.40 billion), so the funding paid sits on a large base of money. Liquidations in the last 24 hours totaled 1,272 on Bitcoin with 12.5 million USD in long wipeouts versus 1.9 million in shorts, and 1,529 on Ethereum with 13.75 million in longs underwater versus 4.18 million in shorts. Long liquidations are running 6.6 to 3.3 times heavier than short ones across the board. The market is testing long holders.

The physical flows tell a story of caution paired with leverage supply. Whales moved 60.2 million USD of Bitcoin off exchanges in the last 24 hours (net outflow), a move toward cold storage that historically suggests conviction. But the bigger picture is the stablecoin traffic: USDT and USDC are being moved onto Binance and Deribit in extraordinary size, with the two largest single inflows being nearly 500 million USD each into Binance. The net stablecoin buying power is negative 36.8 million USD, meaning outflows of stables exceed inflows on a net basis, but the venue-level concentration (derivative venues receiving fresh dollars) indicates leverage capacity is being built into derivatives markets. Over the last five sessions, Bitcoin ETF flows have persisted positive with 865.3 million USD net (same direction for five days), and Ethereum shows 243.7 million USD net positive over the same window, but only four same-direction days. This is bid support from traditional finance, steady but not accelerating.

The Fear and Greed gauge sits at 30, labeled as Fear, within a 30-day range of 22 to 33. The crowd is nervous and has been for weeks. That fear is matched by the tape: negative price action, large drawdowns from peaks, elevated volatility, and liquidations concentrated on the long side. Yet the sentiment is also narrower than the positioning. Funding is still positive; long-to-short ratios are still extreme; and ETF flows are still constructive. This gap between what the crowd feels and what the leverage market is doing is the central tension. One side is preparing for further downside with either short selling or storage moves; the other is betting on a rebound and paying 11% annualized for the privilege. The positioning is not fragile yet, but it is neither cheap nor defensive.

Watch for a breakdown in the 5-session ETF flow streak, a reversal of the daily whale flow (coins moving back onto exchanges), or a sustained flip in Bitcoin's MACD below signal line. A serious test would be fresh long liquidations exceeding 15 to 20 million USD on Bitcoin in a single 24-hour window, signaling that the leverage construction is beginning to crack. Until one of those conditions appears, the tape shows a bear market at rest, not in retreat.
